facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s with a history of hypertension
sudden-onset chest pain
no history of any acute febrile illness
no family history of sudden cardiac death
tachycardic with a pulse of 120 beats/min
blood pressure was normal
White blood cell count: 14,300/µL
Serum calcium: within normal limits
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
Initial ECG showed sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, PR-segment depression in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 to V6
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm

concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, tachycardia, and elevated troponin and brain-type natriuretic peptide levels, which are consistent with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
The patient has an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass, which is suggestive of pheochromocytoma.
The patient presented with chest pain and elevated troponin levels, which are consistent with myocardial infarction.
The patient presented with chest pain, tachycardia, and elevated troponin levels, which are consistent with acute coronary syndrome.
The patient has an adrenal mass, which could be causing adrenal insufficiency.
The patient has an elevated white blood cell count, which is suggestive of sepsis.
The patient has a history of hypertension and presented with normal blood pressure, but could be at risk for hypertensive emergency.
The patient presented with elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide levels and ECG changes, which could be consistent with cardiac tamponade.

rationales.F10: Elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide levels are indicative of heart failure, which can be caused by myocardial infarction and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F11: ECG findings are consistent with myocardial infarction and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F12: The presence of an adrenal mass is suggestive of pheochromocytoma.
